BATCH D · BOARD 4 OF 6

Lab operations

Screens 12–14 and 20. "The reagent had expired" and "someone else had the machine" are the two most common reasons an experiment did not happen. Inventory, storage, booking and the SOP library exist so those two sentences become records rather than excuses — and so a lot number links a physical vial to a failure taxonomy branch.

EXPIRED, NOT DELETED
An expired item stays in the list, in red, until someone physically disposes of it and records that. Hiding it means the next person finds a vial the system says does not exist.
LOT IS A FIRST-CLASS FIELD
Two rows share a catalogue number because they are different lots — and one is implicated in an open issue and six validation reports. This is the join between a physical shelf and the failure taxonomy.
USED IN
Every item counts the notebook entries that consumed it. When a result looks wrong, the first question is what went into it — and that column answers it in one click.

THE MAP IS A CLAIM, NOT A TRUTH
It shows the date it was last checked against the actual freezer, and marks three positions as disputed where the record and a recent scan disagree. A storage map nobody has verified is worse than no map, because people stop opening the drawer.
RESERVED POSITIONS
Six positions are held for the p8 banking task. Reserving is part of the task checklist, so twenty vials never arrive at a full box at 6pm on a Friday.

THIS IS WHAT ISSUE #39 IS ABOUT
You are first on the waitlist for Tuesday 14–16. Booking is not the bottleneck — a three-week service window is, and the issue tracker holds that fact rather than the calendar.
A booking creates a task at the same times and links it to the project, so the calendar and the board never disagree about what you are doing on Tuesday. Training sign-off is checked at booking, not at the door.

WHAT AN EXPIRED SIGN-OFF DOES
Your LN2 refresher lapsed 11 days ago and task T-0518 needs it. The task is not deleted or silently reassigned — it shows the blocker and offers the 20-minute refresher. Blocking work invisibly is how safety systems get routed around.

GHS HAZARDS · SUBSTANCES IN THIS PROTOCOL
!
DMSO
GHS07 · carries solutes through skin. Change nitrile gloves on contact.
❄
Liquid nitrogen
Cryogenic burns, asphyxiation. Face shield, cryo gloves, O₂ monitor.
☣
Lentiviral particles
Class II cabinet, dedicated waste, 1% hypochlorite 30 min.
The assessment is attached to the method card, not filed separately — so it travels with every fork of that protocol into every other lab, and a fork that introduces a new substance is flagged as needing a fresh assessment before it can be published.
